maya: Quick heads-up — Q3 hosted demand forecast just shifted after the new embed customers onboarded. We're looking at a potential reserved capacity gap if we don't hedge.
maya: Short summary: committed reserved GPUs (monthly equivalent) = 80; model-driven baseline demand = 120; projected peak buffer (95th pct) = 150. Gap = ~70 GPUs against peak, ~40 vs committed baseline. Need to decide a low-risk hedging plan by EOD Friday.
nick: Can you share the region split? we should avoid blanket buys across all regions.
maya: Region breakout (30d moving avg -> Q3 projection):
```
us-west: committed 40, forecast 65 (+25)
eu: committed 25, forecast 35 (+10)
apac: committed 15, forecast 20 (+5)
```
Total: committed 80 -> forecast 120 (+40). Peak buffer request pushes to 150 in spikes.
jeremy: Rough cost check: what's the incremental monthly $ if we buy reserved vs rely on ondemand/spot? quick calc below (ballpark):
```
Option A) short-term reserved (1mo) add 40 gpus: $/gpu/mo = $2,400 -> extra = $96k/mo
Option B) ondemand + spot mix: weighted avg $/gpu/hr = $3.2 -> 40*24*30*3.2 =~ $92k/mo but volatile
Option C) commit 12mo smaller, discount applies but long term risk
```
Numbers are placeholders — finance export will have exact unit prices.
finance-bot: Billing export for last 90d (per-region, per-instance): https://billing.redwood.internal/exports/2026-03-gpu-usage.csv :eyes:
tara: Two pragmatic options I prefer: 1) short rolling 30-day reserved in us-west for +25 GPUs (largest delta) + autoscaler policy tweak to spill to apac eu secondaries, or 2) negotiate a blended reserved with cloud partner for a flexible pool (can shift regions) — both lower risk than a 12mo commit.
nick: I like 30-day for us-west only and use spot fallback for 15-20% of load. How would this affect our SLA / lat p95? if we move some customers to eu fallback we need to measure extra p95.
maya: Good call. Estimated p95 increase if eu fallback used for 20% of requests: +25-45ms on average, peaky models +80ms occasionally. Customer-impact acceptable for non-critical routes. We'll pin critical routes to reserved capacity.
ops-bot: Quick checklist proposal: 
- [ ] Create short-term reserved order for 25 GPUs in us-west (ops)
- [ ] Update autoscaler policies: prefer reserved pool, allow cross-region spill (eng-runtime)
- [ ] Configure route-level pinning for critical tenants (product)
- [ ] Finance to validate unit rates and approve purchase (finance)
jeremy: One more data ask: show committed coverage ratio across models (tokens-per-gpu). I'll run a join on the eval -> usage table. Expect that embed-heavy models have 2.6x GPU-time per 1k tokens vs chat models.
finance-bot: FYI — if we place a 30-day reservation, cloud provider charges are prorated daily but non-refundable. Also available is a "regional convertible" option with 5% premium that allows region migration within 30d.
tara: Let's also test a smaller experiment: reserve 10 GPUs for burst pool in eu for 14d to validate cross-region failover and latency changes. If p95 delta <50ms we'll scale further.
maya: Proposed action timeline:
- Today: approve us-west 25 GPU 30-day reservation (ops + finance)
- Tomorrow: autoscaler policy PR and canary cross-region routing (eng-runtime)
- 14d: validate metrics (latency, cost coverage, utilization)
- 30d: reassess and either roll forward or purchase convertible pool
nick: +1. Please include a dashboard widget that shows committed vs actual utilization (per-model) and projected runway so we can avoid underutilization surprises.
ops-bot: Created ticket INFRA-1249 for the reservation + autoscaler changes. Assigning to @maya, @tara. ETA for PR: 24h.
maya: I'll open the finance approval PR and attach the billing export. tagging @finance for sign-off. :thumbsup:
jeremy: I'll prepare the coverage-by-model CSV and drop in the ticket. also will run a smoke test for eu fallback tonight.
maya: Thanks everyone — let's keep this tight. if we can't land the short-term reserve we'll fallback to spot + throttling for low-priority routes and trigger a product notice window.
